title: Argument and debate
objectives: Structure a spoken opinion with una, ikalawa, panghuli and sa kabuuan
Rebut an opposing view politely with hindi ako sang-ayon dahil... and may punto ka, pero...
Execute the concession-then-counter move fluently in real time
Moderate and participate in a panel-style discussion

grammar.title: The skeleton of a spoken opinion
grammar.explanation:
A B2 opinion has announced structure — the listener always knows where you are. Open by staking the claim: Sa aking palagay / Para sa akin / Naniniwala ako na... Then number the reasons: Una, ... Ikalawa, ... Ikatlo, ... at panghuli, ... Close by zooming out: Sa kabuuan (on the whole), Kaya naman (which is why), Sa huli (in the end).

Support each point before leaving it: Halimbawa, ... 'for example'; Ayon nga sa pag-aaral, ... 'as the study indeed says' (note nga leaning on the authority); Makikita natin ito sa... 'we can see this in...'.

English speakers under pressure tend to dump their reasons in one unstructured breath. Tagalog listeners, like English ones, hold on to signposts — and in a debate, the signposts also buy you planning time. Una pause ... gives you a full second to compose point one. Use the machinery; that is what it is for.

grammar.title: Agreeing, disagreeing, and the polite rebuttal
grammar.explanation:
Full agreement: Sang-ayon ako / Sumasang-ayon ako sa sinabi ni Ana. Partial: May punto ka 'you have a point', Tama ka sa isang banda 'you're right in one respect'. Disagreement scales by bluntness: Hindi ako (lubos na) sang-ayon 'I don't (fully) agree' → Iba ang pananaw ko 'my view differs' → Mali iyan 'that's wrong' (combative — save it for close friends or actual debates).

The rebuttal formula: acknowledge, then attack the reasoning, not the person. Hindi ako sang-ayon, dahil hindi sinasabi ng datos iyan — 'I disagree, because the data doesn't say that.' Add naman to soften: Hindi naman sa mali ka, pero... 'It's not that you're wrong, but...'. Question the premise with kung and ba: Pero kung totoo iyan, bakit patuloy na tumataas ang bilang? — 'But if that's true, why do the numbers keep rising?'

The strongest B2 move is concession-then-counter, now performed live: Totoo na mas mura ang imported na bigas — aminado ako diyan. Pero ang tanong: ano ang mangyayari sa ating mga magsasaka? You met the written version in Unit 4; in speech, deliver the concession in a calm tone and let pero carry the turn.

grammar.title: Panel language: holding, yielding, and stealing the floor
grammar.explanation:
Discussions need traffic control. To take the floor politely: Kung maaari, gusto kong magdagdag 'if I may, I'd like to add'; Sandali lang, may punto lang ako rito 'just a moment, I have a point here'. To hold it against interruption: Patapusin mo muna ako 'let me finish first' — the pa- causative of tapos, literally 'let me be finished'; softer: Konting pasensya, papunta na ako diyan 'bear with me, I'm getting there'.

To yield: Ikaw naman 'your turn'; Ano sa palagay mo? 'what do you think?'. A moderator distributes turns with kay: Kay Atty. Reyes naman tayo — 'Over to Atty. Reyes.' and manages time: Isang minuto na lang po 'one minute left'; Pakiikli na lang po ang sagot 'please keep the answer short' — note the paki- request form doing polite crowd control.

Meta-comments keep debate civil: Wag nating personalin 'let's not make it personal'; Balik tayo sa isyu 'back to the issue'; Magkaiba tayo ng opinyon, pero pareho tayo ng layunin 'we differ in opinion but share the goal' — the standard graceful close between opponents.

vocab.note: variants: sa palagay ko, sa tingin ko, para sa akin

example.tl: Sa aking palagay, masyadong maaga pa para magdesisyon.
example.en: In my opinion, it's still too early to decide.

example.tl: Naniniwala akong kaya nating ayusin ito nang sama-sama.
example.en: I believe we can fix this together.

example.tl: Iba ang pananaw ng kabataan tungkol sa trabaho.
example.en: Young people have a different perspective on work.

example.tl: Una, mahal ito; ikalawa, hindi natin kailangan.
example.en: First, it's expensive; second, we don't need it.

example.tl: Panghuli, dapat isaalang-alang ang kapakanan ng mga bata.
example.en: Lastly, the children's welfare must be considered.

example.tl: Sa kabuuan, mas marami ang benepisyo kaysa sa panganib.
example.en: On the whole, the benefits outnumber the risks.

example.tl: Sang-ayon ako sa unang punto, pero hindi sa ikalawa.
example.en: I agree with the first point, but not the second.

example.tl: May punto ka, pero may nakalimutan kang detalye.
example.en: You have a point, but you forgot a detail.

example.tl: Hindi naman sa ayaw ko; kulang lang talaga ang badyet.
example.en: It's not that I don't want to; the budget is just really short.

example.tl: Mahina ang katwiran niya dahil walang ebidensya.
example.en: His reasoning is weak because there's no evidence.

example.tl: Magpakita ka ng ebidensya bago ka mang-akusa.
example.en: Show evidence before you accuse.

example.tl: Ano ang sinasabi ng datos tungkol sa kaso ng dengue?
example.en: What does the data say about dengue cases?

example.tl: Ayon sa isang pag-aaral, nakakatulong ang idlip sa memorya.
example.en: According to one study, naps help memory.

example.tl: Gusto ko lang magdagdag ng isang maikling punto.
example.en: I'd just like to add one brief point.

example.tl: Patapusin ninyo muna ang nagsasalita bago sumagot.
example.en: Let the speaker finish first before responding.

example.tl: Sumagot siya nang mahinahon sa mabigat na tanong.
example.en: She answered the heavy question calmly.

example.tl: Nanatiling mahinahon ang moderator sa gitna ng sigawan.
example.en: The moderator stayed composed amid the shouting.

example.tl: Marunong siyang mangatwiran nang hindi nakakasakit.

example.tl: Sa huli, nanaig ang mas mahinahong panig.

example.tl: Timbangin natin ang benepisyo at ang panganib.

dialogue.title: Debate sa radyo: apat na araw na trabaho?
dialogue.context: A radio host moderates a short debate between a labor advocate and a business owner about a proposed four-day work week.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.tl: Magandang umaga sa inyong lahat. Ang isyu natin ngayon: dapat bang gawing apat na araw ang isang linggo ng trabaho? Kay Ginang Salazar muna tayo.
lines.en: Good morning, everyone. Our issue today: should the work week be made four days? Let's go to Mrs. Salazar first.

lines.speaker: Salazar
lines.tl: Salamat po. Naniniwala akong dapat. Una, ayon sa mga pag-aaral, mas produktibo ang mga manggagawang may sapat na pahinga. Ikalawa, makakatipid sila sa pamasahe. At panghuli, mas marami silang oras para sa pamilya.
lines.en: Thank you. I believe we should. First, according to studies, workers with enough rest are more productive. Second, they save on fares. And lastly, they have more time for family.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.tl: Malinaw na tatlong punto. Ginoong Chua, ano po ang tugon ninyo?
lines.en: Three clear points. Mr. Chua, your response?

lines.speaker: Chua
lines.tl: May punto si Ginang Salazar tungkol sa pahinga — aminado ako diyan. Pero hindi ako sang-ayon sa kabuuan, dahil hindi kakayanin ng maliliit na negosyo ang parehong sahod sa mas kaunting araw.
lines.en: Mrs. Salazar has a point about rest — I'll admit that. But I disagree overall, because small businesses can't afford the same pay for fewer days.

lines.speaker: Salazar
lines.tl: Kung maaari, gusto kong sumagot diyan. Sa mga bansang sumubok nito, hindi naman bumagsak ang mga negosyo. Ang datos —
lines.en: If I may, I'd like to respond to that. In the countries that tried it, businesses didn't collapse. The data —

lines.speaker: Chua
lines.tl: Pero ibang ekonomiya ang mga bansang iyon! Dito sa atin —
lines.en: But those countries have different economies! Here —

lines.speaker: Salazar
lines.tl: Patapusin mo muna ako, Ginoong Chua. Ang datos mula sa mga pilot program dito mismo sa Pilipinas ay nagpapakita ng parehong resulta.
lines.en: Let me finish first, Mr. Chua. Data from pilot programs here in the Philippines itself shows the same result.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.tl: Isa-isa lang po tayo. Ginoong Chua, ikaw naman.
lines.en: One at a time, please. Mr. Chua, your turn.

lines.speaker: Chua
lines.tl: Pasensya na po. Hindi naman sa ayaw ko ng pahinga para sa mga manggagawa. Ang akin lang: timbangin muna natin ang benepisyo at panganib bago gawing batas.
lines.en: My apologies. It's not that I don't want rest for workers. My only point: let's weigh the benefits and risks before making it law.

lines.speaker: Salazar
lines.tl: Diyan po tayo nagkakasundo. Magkaiba man kami ng pananaw, pareho kami ng layunin: ang kapakanan ng manggagawa at ng negosyo.
lines.en: There we agree. Though our views differ, we share a goal: the welfare of both workers and businesses.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.tl: Mahinahong pagtatapos — bihira sa radyo! Sa kabuuan, dalawang matibay na panig. Kayo na po ang humusga, mga tagapakinig.
lines.en: A calm ending — rare on radio! On the whole, two strong sides. You be the judge, dear listeners.

reading.title: Kolum: Bakit ako bumoto ng hindi sa curfew ng kabataan
reading.tl:
Noong isang linggo, bumoto ang aming konseho tungkol sa panukalang curfew para sa mga menor de edad: bawal lumabas ng bahay mula alas-diyes ng gabi hanggang alas-kuwatro ng umaga. Labing-isa ang bumoto ng oo. Ako ang nag-iisang hindi. Hayaan ninyong ipaliwanag ko.

Una, walang malinaw na ebidensya na nakakabawas ng krimen ang curfew. Sa mga lungsod na nagpatupad nito, ayon sa mga pag-aaral, hindi bumaba ang bilang ng mga krimeng sangkot ang kabataan; lumipat lamang ang oras ng mga ito. Kung ang layunin ay kaligtasan, dapat nating tugunan ang ugat: ang kawalan ng masisilungan, ang droga, at ang kahirapan.

Ikalawa, hindi patas ang pagpapatupad. Aminin natin: ang anak ng mayaman na hatinggabing umuuwi mula sa party ay ihahatid ng sariling kotse; ang anak ng mahirap na umuuwi mula sa trabaho sa gabi ang huhulihin sa kalsada. Sa madaling salita, ang batas na ito ay parusa sa kahirapan, hindi sa krimen.

Ikatlo — at ito ang pinakamahalaga sa akin — mali ang mensahe nito sa ating mga kabataan: na sila ay panganib na dapat ikulong, sa halip na mamamayang dapat kalingain.

May punto ang aking mga kasamahan nang sabihin nilang nag-aalala ang mga magulang. Totoo iyan, at hindi ko iyon binabalewala. Ngunit ang pag-aalala ay hindi sapat na batayan ng batas; ebidensya ang kailangan. Sa kabuuan, bumoto ako ng hindi sapagkat naniniwala akong ang tunay na kaligtasan ay hindi nakukuha sa pagkukulong ng kabataan sa bahay, kundi sa pagbuo ng pamayanang ligtas para sa lahat, anumang oras.
reading.en:
Last week, our council voted on a proposed curfew for minors: no leaving the house from ten in the evening to four in the morning. Eleven voted yes. I was the lone no. Allow me to explain.

First, there is no clear evidence that curfews reduce crime. In the cities that implemented them, according to studies, the number of crimes involving youth did not fall; only their timing shifted. If the goal is safety, we should address the roots: the lack of shelters, drugs, and poverty.

Second, enforcement is not fair. Let's admit it: the rich family's child coming home at midnight from a party will be driven home in the family car; the poor family's child coming home from a night job is the one who will be picked up on the street. In short, this law punishes poverty, not crime.

Third — and this matters most to me — it sends the wrong message to our young people: that they are a danger to be locked up, rather than citizens to be cared for.

My colleagues had a point when they said parents are worried. That is true, and I do not dismiss it. But worry is not a sufficient basis for law; evidence is what's needed. On the whole, I voted no because I believe real safety is not achieved by locking young people in their houses, but by building a community that is safe for everyone, at any hour.

exercises.prompt: Which sequence correctly signposts a three-point opinion?
exercises.explain: Una / ikalawa / (ikatlo) / panghuli number the points of an argument. The others are irrealis words, time words, and cause-purpose connectors.

exercises.prompt: Sa ___, mas marami ang benepisyo kaysa sa panganib, kaya sang-ayon ako. (on the whole)
exercises.hint: the zoom-out phrase before a conclusion
exercises.explain: Sa kabuuan 'on the whole / in summary' signals you are wrapping up and weighing everything said.

exercises.prompt: Someone rebuts you: 'May punto ka, pero hindi iyan sinasabi ng datos.' What did they just do?
choices: Conceded partially, then attacked your evidence
exercises.explain: May punto ka concedes; pero + hindi iyan sinasabi ng datos counters by challenging the evidence — the concession-then-counter move, aimed at the reasoning, not the person.

exercises.prompt: ___ mo muna ako bago ka sumagot — hindi pa tapos ang punto ko. (Let me finish)
exercises.explain: Patapusin mo (muna) ako = 'let me finish first' — the standard floor-holding phrase, built with the pa- -in causative.

exercises.prompt: As moderator you need shorter answers. The polite phrase is:
choices: Pakiikli na lang po ang sagot.
Wala nang oras, umuwi na tayo.
exercises.explain: Paki- + ikli forms the polite request 'please shorten (your answer)' — moderator's crowd control without rudeness.

exercises.tl: Hindi naman sa ayaw ko sa panukala; gusto ko lang munang makita ang datos bago tayo magpasya.
choices: They don't reject the proposal outright; they just want to see data before deciding.
They completely reject the proposal and the data.
They already decided to support the proposal.
They want to decide first and look at data later.
exercises.explain: Hindi naman sa ayaw ko softens the objection: not refusal, but a request to see the datos first. Bago tayo magpasya = 'before we decide'.

exercises.prompt: I don't agree, because the study doesn't say that.
exercises.answer: Hindi ako sang-ayon, dahil hindi iyan sinasabi ng pag-aaral.
accept: Hindi ako sang-ayon, dahil hindi iyan sinasabi ng pag-aaral
Hindi ako sang-ayon dahil hindi sinasabi ng pag-aaral iyan
Hindi ako sumasang-ayon, dahil hindi iyan sinasabi ng pag-aaral
exercises.explain: Hindi ako sang-ayon states the disagreement; dahil + the evidence-based reason attacks the claim, not the claimant.

exercises.prompt: Magkaiba man tayo ng pananaw, pareho naman tayo ng layunin.
exercises.answer: Though we differ in viewpoint, we share the same goal.
accept: Though we differ in viewpoint, we share the same goal
Even if our views are different, our goal is the same
We may have different perspectives, but we have the same objective
exercises.explain: The graceful debate close: man after magkaiba concedes the difference; pareho tayo ng layunin affirms common ground.

exercises.prompt: From the reading: what is the columnist's SECOND reason for voting no?
choices: Curfews have been proven to raise crime.
Enforcement would fall unfairly on poor youth.
The curfew hours are too short.
exercises.explain: Ikalawa, hindi patas ang pagpapatupad: the rich child gets driven home while the poor child working nights gets picked up — the law punishes poverty.

exercises.prompt: The columnist writes: 'May punto ang aking mga kasamahan... Totoo iyan... Ngunit ang pag-aalala ay hindi sapat na batayan ng batas.' Which debate move is this?
exercises.explain: The colleagues' point (parental worry) is granted as true, then countered on principle: worry is not a sufficient basis for law. Classic concede-then-counter.

exercises.tl: Sandali lang po, gusto ko lang magdagdag ng isang maikling punto bago tayo bumoto.
choices: To add one brief point before the vote
To repeat the previous speaker's point
To leave the meeting before the vote
exercises.explain: Sandali lang po asks for the floor; magdagdag ng isang maikling punto = 'add one brief point'; bago tayo bumoto = 'before we vote'.

exercises.prompt: First, it is expensive. Second, there is no evidence that it works. Therefore, I am voting no.
exercises.answer: Una, mahal ito. Ikalawa, walang ebidensya na gumagana ito. Kaya naman, boboto ako ng hindi.
accept: Una, mahal ito. Ikalawa, walang ebidensya na gumagana ito. Kaya naman, boboto ako ng hindi
Una, mahal ito. Ikalawa, walang ebidensyang gumagana ito. Kaya boboto ako ng hindi
Una, mahal ito. Pangalawa, walang ebidensya na gumagana ito. Samakatuwid, boboto ako ng hindi
exercises.explain: Numbered signposts (una, ikalawa/pangalawa) organize the reasons; kaya naman or samakatuwid draws the conclusion — the full skeleton of a spoken opinion.
